author: AMAW
title: WE CALL FOR ANARCHIST PARTICIPATION
content:
WE CALL FOR ANARCHIST PARTICIPATION IN:

–> Manifestation against the Militarization of the Health Sector – 10.07. – 14:00 to 16:00 @ DRK Kliniken, Osloer Str. 36

–> Demonstration „Wedding ohne Waffen! Gemeinsam gegen Krieg!“ – 11.07. – 14 Uhr @ S+U Gesundbrunnen (in the Antifa Block)

The Antimilitarist Assembly Wedding is an anarchist assembly, meaning anti-authoritarian, anti-nationalist, and horizontal: it’s open to anyone who wants to take action against war and the military-industrial complex behind it.

What pushed us to organize the assembly was learning that Rheinmetall, Germany’s biggest arms manufacturer, was going to start producing weapons‘ components here in our neighborhood.

The 8th of July is the first day of this shift: from this day on Rheinmetall’s workers are manufacturing parts necessary for the production of tank ammunition, artillery systems, and armored vehicles.

It is important to ask ourselves: why here? Why now?

It’s not by chance that a weapons manufacturer is now operating in our neighborhood. In the name of public safety, Wedding has been already militarized: we can’t walk a few meters without seeing a police van, young people are constantly stopped and searched by the cops, Leopoldplatz is now a Waffenverbot zone: please open your bag so we can check you don’t have a knife on you, but also enjoy these locally produced bio-bullets!

And let’s not forget that, back in March, the house on Schererstr. where we and other groups meet and organize, was raided.

These measures strengthen the narrative of Wedding as a territory that needs to be tamed: not just to ensure safety but to make way for economic development. Development for whom? Safety for whom?

What we are seeing happening here is happening all over Europe, where a narrative of permanent danger is used to justify the idea that billions are needed to defend the country against internal and external enemies.

For those who join the struggle against wars, occupation and militarization, and against the chilling normalization of three years of live-streamed genocide against the Palestinians, repression is not a matter of if but when. As the show trials against the Ulm 5 and Daniela Klette show, while the technologies of repression become more sophisticated, its tactics are old: intimidation, surveillance, abuse and incarceration. Painting people as „extremists“ and therefore a danger to a society that is now being asked to, and later will be forced to, send its children to war.

And yes, we are all their enemies because we refuse to accept that state violence and wars are the only answer. We refuse to accept the normalization of surveillance, repression, and the criminalization of anyone who dares to fight back.

Please, don’t be fooled by the old story of the ‚bad militant‘ versus the ‚good activist‘. We are all good activists until the state decides that we are terrorists.

But who is guilty of killing thousands all over the world through war, dispossession, and man-made disasters? Who is responsible for enforcing a border regime that pushes thousands of people each year to their death?

The only terrorist is the state. And as any abuser, it wants us to be complicit with the violence it inflicts: whether by propaganda or coercion, we are being forced to accept that all public resources need to be redirected towards war, that money is needed for tanks and bombs instead of education, healthcare and an already shitty, already punitive welfare system.

Everyone can be drafted: if not as a soldier, for the infrastructure of war. Are you a doctor? Congratulations, now you’re a doctor for injured soldiers. Are you unemployed? Congratulations, now you work in a weapons factory. Do you work in IT? Congratulations! Now you’re training AI to search for deserters.

We are supposed to quietly accept a number of things: the ASOG police law reform and AI-powered surveillance making it possible to spy on virtually anyone. That deportations and de-naturalization are also used as threats against organizing politically, and which additionally unleash more racist violence. We are supposed to believe that defending the ‚eastern flank‘ justifies any measure: from cuts to anything but military spending, to conscription, to turning all critical infrastructure into hubs to support the logistics of war.

And we are supposed to welcome an arms factory here where we live and work and raise our kids.

We don’t want weapons produced here or anywhere else! We don’t want to be complicit in a system that oppresses us and that kills in countries made into permanent war zones. Let’s be clear: before and after the farce of peace conferences and ceasefires, war never really stops, and what they call peace is only compliance with the status quo. But there is no peace on stolen land! And all the land is stolen when profits and dividends come before people. All land is stolen until the last prison is burned to the ground, until the last border is abolished, and as long as the maintenance of this so-called first world depends on a colonial and genocidal project. And we must always remember what is tested in war zones will always come back to bite us in the ass.

And what we are witnessing today is indeed a test: How long can the state keep up with the fiction of a democratic order? While homes and meeting places are searched for daring to say ’no‘ to war and militarization? While people are stripped of their citizenship because of a post on social media? While our comrades Zo, Leandra, Vi, Daniel and Crow are being subjected to a farce trial in Stammheim, the same place as the RAF?

Only last month, Akel D., a student of Wedding’s Berliner Hochschule fuer Technik was killed in Lebanon by an Israeli airstrike while visiting family, and the initiative to remember him and end university’s cooperation with apartheid was immediately subjected to surveillance and intimidation.

This is a test for all of us too: how much can we take? How long can we pretend that as long as we protest, but not too loud, we will be safe? That if we comply with the new normal, nothing will happen to us?

It’s time to say no! To turn solidarity into action! No conscription for our youth! No weapons for genocide! No police in our neighborhoods! Solidarity with the Ulm5 and free Palestine!

Let’s take to the streets – today, tomorrow, every day.

Self-organize! Desert! Sabotage!

WIR RUFEN ZUR ANARCHISTISCHEN BETEILIGUNG AUF:

–> Demonstration gegen die Militarisierung des Gesundheitswesens – 10.07. – 14:00 bis 16:00 Uhr bei den DRK-Kliniken, Osloer Str. 36

–> Demonstration „Wedding ohne Waffen! Gemeinsam gegen Krieg!“ – 11.07. – 14 Uhr am S+U Gesundbrunnen (im Antifa-Block)

Die Antimilitaristische Versammlung Wedding ist eine anarchistische Versammlung, das heißt antiautoritär, antinationalistisch und horizontal: Sie steht Allen offen, die gegen den Krieg und den dahinter stehenden militärisch-industriellen Komplex aktiv werden wollen.

Was uns dazu bewogen hat, die Versammlung zu organisieren, war die Nachricht, dass Rheinmetall, Deutschlands größter Rüstungskonzern, hier in unserem Viertel mit der Produktion von Waffenkomponenten beginnen wird.

Der 8. Juli ist der erste Tag dieser Umstellung: Ab diesem Tag fertigen die Arbeiter*innen von Rheinmetall Teile, die für die Herstellung von Panzermunition, Artilleriesystemen und gepanzerten Fahrzeugen benötigt werden.

Es ist wichtig, uns zu fragen: Warum hier? Warum jetzt?

Es ist kein Zufall, dass nun ein Rüstungsunternehmen in unserem Viertel produziert. Im Namen der öffentlichen Sicherheit wurde Wedding bereits militarisiert: Wir können kaum ein paar Meter gehen, ohne ein Polizeiauto zu sehen, junge Menschen werden ständig von der Polizei angehalten und durchsucht und der Leopoldplatz ist nun eine Waffenverbotszone: „Bitte öffnen Sie Ihre Tasche, damit wir überprüfen können, ob Sie kein Messer bei sich haben – aber genießen Sie gerne die lokal produzierten Bio-Kugeln!“

Und nicht zu vergessen: Im März wurde das Haus in der Schererstraße, in dem wir und andere Gruppen uns treffen und organisieren, durchsucht.

Diese Maßnahmen untermauern das Narrativ, dass Wedding ein Gebiet sei, das gezähmt werden muss – nicht nur, um Sicherheit zu gewährleisten, sondern auch, um Platz für wirtschaftliche Entwicklung zu schaffen. Entwicklung für wen? Sicherheit für wen?

Was wir hier beobachten, geschieht überall in Europa, wo ein Narrativ der permanenten Gefahr herangezogen wird, um die Idee zu rechtfertigen, dass Milliarden benötigt werden, um das Land gegen innere und äußere Feinde zu verteidigen.

Für diejenigen, die sich dem Kampf gegen Kriege, Besatzung und Militarisierung sowie gegen die erschreckende Normalisierung des seit drei Jahren live übertragenen Völkermords an den Palästinensern anschließen, ist Repression keine Frage von „Ob“, sondern „Wann“. Wie die Schauprozesse gegen die „Ulm 5“ und Daniela Klette zeigen: Während die Technologien der Repression immer ausgefeilter werden, sind ihre Taktiken altbekannt: Einschüchterung, Überwachung, Misshandlung und Inhaftierung. Menschen werden als „Extremist*innen“ dargestellt und damit als Gefahr für eine Gesellschaft, die jetzt aufgefordert wird – und später gezwungen sein wird –, ihre Kinder in den Krieg zu schicken.

Und ja, wir Alle sind ihre Feinde, weil wir uns weigern zu akzeptieren, dass staatliche Gewalt und Kriege die einzige Antwort sind. Wir weigern uns, die Normalisierung von Überwachung, Unterdrückung und die Kriminalisierung all derer hinzunehmen die es wagen, sich zu wehren.

Bitte lasst euch nicht von der alten Geschichte von „böse*n Militante*n“ im Gegensatz zu „gute*n Aktivist*in“ täuschen. Wir sind alle gute Aktivist*innen, bis der Staat beschließt, dass wir Terrorist*innen sind.

Aber wer ist schuldig am Tod von tausenden Menschen auf der ganzen Welt durch Krieg, Enteignung und von Menschen verursachte Katastrophen? Wer ist verantwortlich für die Durchsetzung eines Grenzregimes, das jedes Jahr tausende Menschen in den Tod treibt?

Der einzige Terrorist ist der Staat. Und wie jeder Täter, möchte er, dass wir uns mitschuldig machen, an der Gewalt, die er ausübt: Ob durch Propaganda oder Zwang – wir werden dazu gezwungen zu akzeptieren, dass alle öffentlichen Mittel in den Krieg umgeleitet werden müssen, dass Geld für Panzer und Bomben statt für Bildung, Gesundheitsversorgung und ein ohnehin schon beschissenes, ohnehin schon strafendes Sozialsystem benötigt wird.

Jeder kann eingezogen werden: wenn nicht als Soldat*in, dann für die Infrastruktur des Krieges. Bist du Arzt*in? Herzlichen Glückwunsch, jetzt bist du Arzt*in für verwundete Soldat*innen. Bist du arbeitslos? Herzlichen Glückwunsch, jetzt arbeitest du in einer Waffenfabrik. Arbeitest du in der IT? Herzlichen Glückwunsch! Jetzt trainierst du KI darauf, nach Deserteur*innen zu suchen.

Wir sollen eine Reihe von Dingen stillschweigend hinnehmen: die ASOG-Polizeireform und die KI-gestützte Überwachung, die es ermöglicht, praktisch jede*n auszuspionieren. Dass Abschiebungen und Entzug der Staatsbürgerschaft auch als Drohung gegen politisches Aktiv werden eingesetzt werden und darüber hinaus noch mehr rassistische Gewalt auslösen. Wir sollen glauben, dass die Verteidigung der „Ostflanke“ jede Maßnahme rechtfertigt: von Kürzungen bei allen Ausgaben außer den Militärausgaben über die Wehrpflicht bis hin zur Umwandlung aller kritischen Infrastrukturen in Knotenpunkte zur Unterstützung der Kriegslogistik.

Und wir sollen eine Waffenfabrik willkommen heißen, hier, wo wir leben, arbeiten und unsere Kinder großziehen.

Wir wollen keine Waffenproduktion, weder hier noch anderswo! Wir wollen uns nicht mitschuldig machen an einem System, das uns unterdrückt und das in Ländern, die zu permanenten Kriegsgebieten gemacht wurden, Menschen tötet. Um es klar zu sagen: Vor und nach der Farce der Friedenskonferenzen und Waffenstillstände hört der Krieg nie wirklich auf, und was sie Frieden nennen, ist nichts anderes als die Aufrechterhaltung des Status quo. Jedes Land ist gestohlen, bis das letzte Gefängnis niedergebrannt ist, bis die letzte Grenze abgeschafft ist und solange die Aufrechterhaltung dieser sogenannten Ersten Welt von einem kolonialen und völkermörderischen Projekt abhängt. Und wir müssen uns stets daran erinnern: Was in Kriegsgebieten erprobt wird, wird immer wieder auf uns zurückfallen und uns in den Arsch beißen.

Was wir heute erleben, ist in der Tat ein Test: Wie lange kann der Staat die Illusion einer demokratischen Ordnung aufrechterhalten? Während Wohnungen und Treffpunkte durchsucht werden, weil man es gewagt hat, „Nein“ zu Krieg und Militarisierung zu sagen? Während Menschen wegen eines Beitrags in den sozialen Medien ihrer Staatsbürgerschaft beraubt werden? Während unsere Genoss*innen Zo, Leandra, Vi, Daniel und Crow in Stammheim, demselben Ort wie die RAF, einem Scheinprozess ausgesetzt sind?

Erst letzten Monat wurde Akel D., ein Student der Berliner Hochschule für Technik in Wedding, bei einem Besuch bei seiner Familie im Libanon durch einen israelischen Luftangriff getötet, und die Initiative, an ihn zu erinnern und die Zusammenarbeit der Hochschule mit der Apartheid zu beenden, wurde sofort überwacht und eingeschüchtert.

Und was wir heute erleben, ist in der Tat eine Bewährungsprobe: Wie lange kann der Staat die Fiktion einer demokratischen Ordnung noch aufrechterhalten? Während Wohnungen und Treffpunkte durchsucht werden, weil man es gewagt hat, „Nein“ zu Krieg und Militarisierung zu sagen? Während Menschen wegen eines Beitrags in den sozialen Medien ihre Staatsbürgerschaft entzogen wird? Während unsere Genoss*innen Zo, Leandra, Vi, Daniel und Crow in Stammheim, genau dort, wo einst die RAF stand, einem Scheinprozess ausgesetzt sind?

Erst letzten Monat wurde Akel D., ein Student der Berliner Hochschule für Technik in Wedding, bei einem Besuch bei seiner Familie im Libanon durch einen israelischen Luftangriff getötet, und die Initiative, an ihn zu erinnern und die Zusammenarbeit der Hochschule mit der Apartheid zu beenden, wurde sofort überwacht und eingeschüchtert.

Das ist auch für uns alle eine Bewährungsprobe: Wie viel können wir ertragen? Wie lange können wir so tun, als wären wir sicher, solange wir protestieren, aber nicht zu laut? Dass uns nichts passieren wird, solange wir uns an die neue Normalität halten?

Es ist Zeit, Nein zu sagen! Solidarität in Taten umzusetzen! Keine Wehrpflicht für unsere Jugend! Keine Waffen für Völkermord! Keine Polizei in unseren Vierteln! Solidarität mit den Ulm5 und ein freies Palästina!

Lasst uns auf die Straße gehen – heute, morgen, jeden Tag.

Selbst organisieren! Desertieren! Sabotieren!

title: WE CALL FOR ANARCHIST PARTICIPATION
content:
WE CALL FOR ANARCHIST PARTICIPATION IN:

–> Manifestation against the Militarization of the Health Sector – 10.07. – 14:00 to 16:00 @ DRK Kliniken, Osloer Str. 36

–> Demonstration „Wedding ohne Waffen! Gemeinsam gegen Krieg!“ – 11.07. – 14 Uhr @ S+U Gesundbrunnen (in the Antifa Block)

The Antimilitarist Assembly Wedding is an anarchist assembly, meaning anti-authoritarian, anti-nationalist, and horizontal: it’s open to anyone who wants to take action against war and the military-industrial complex behind it.

What pushed us to organize the assembly was learning that Rheinmetall, Germany’s biggest arms manufacturer, was going to start producing weapons‘ components here in our neighborhood.

The 8th of July is the first day of this shift: from this day on Rheinmetall’s workers are manufacturing parts necessary for the production of tank ammunition, artillery systems, and armored vehicles.

It is important to ask ourselves: why here? Why now?

It’s not by chance that a weapons manufacturer is now operating in our neighborhood. In the name of public safety, Wedding has been already militarized: we can’t walk a few meters without seeing a police van, young people are constantly stopped and searched by the cops, Leopoldplatz is now a Waffenverbot zone: please open your bag so we can check you don’t have a knife on you, but also enjoy these locally produced bio-bullets!

And let’s not forget that, back in March, the house on Schererstr. where we and other groups meet and organize, was raided.

These measures strengthen the narrative of Wedding as a territory that needs to be tamed: not just to ensure safety but to make way for economic development. Development for whom? Safety for whom?

What we are seeing happening here is happening all over Europe, where a narrative of permanent danger is used to justify the idea that billions are needed to defend the country against internal and external enemies.

For those who join the struggle against wars, occupation and militarization, and against the chilling normalization of three years of live-streamed genocide against the Palestinians, repression is not a matter of if but when. As the show trials against the Ulm 5 and Daniela Klette show, while the technologies of repression become more sophisticated, its tactics are old: intimidation, surveillance, abuse and incarceration. Painting people as „extremists“ and therefore a danger to a society that is now being asked to, and later will be forced to, send its children to war.

And yes, we are all their enemies because we refuse to accept that state violence and wars are the only answer. We refuse to accept the normalization of surveillance, repression, and the criminalization of anyone who dares to fight back.

Please, don’t be fooled by the old story of the ‚bad militant‘ versus the ‚good activist‘. We are all good activists until the state decides that we are terrorists.

But who is guilty of killing thousands all over the world through war, dispossession, and man-made disasters? Who is responsible for enforcing a border regime that pushes thousands of people each year to their death?

The only terrorist is the state. And as any abuser, it wants us to be complicit with the violence it inflicts: whether by propaganda or coercion, we are being forced to accept that all public resources need to be redirected towards war, that money is needed for tanks and bombs instead of education, healthcare and an already shitty, already punitive welfare system.

Everyone can be drafted: if not as a soldier, for the infrastructure of war. Are you a doctor? Congratulations, now you’re a doctor for injured soldiers. Are you unemployed? Congratulations, now you work in a weapons factory. Do you work in IT? Congratulations! Now you’re training AI to search for deserters.

We are supposed to quietly accept a number of things: the ASOG police law reform and AI-powered surveillance making it possible to spy on virtually anyone. That deportations and de-naturalization are also used as threats against organizing politically, and which additionally unleash more racist violence. We are supposed to believe that defending the ‚eastern flank‘ justifies any measure: from cuts to anything but military spending, to conscription, to turning all critical infrastructure into hubs to support the logistics of war.

And we are supposed to welcome an arms factory here where we live and work and raise our kids.

We don’t want weapons produced here or anywhere else! We don’t want to be complicit in a system that oppresses us and that kills in countries made into permanent war zones. Let’s be clear: before and after the farce of peace conferences and ceasefires, war never really stops, and what they call peace is only compliance with the status quo. But there is no peace on stolen land! And all the land is stolen when profits and dividends come before people. All land is stolen until the last prison is burned to the ground, until the last border is abolished, and as long as the maintenance of this so-called first world depends on a colonial and genocidal project. And we must always remember what is tested in war zones will always come back to bite us in the ass.

And what we are witnessing today is indeed a test: How long can the state keep up with the fiction of a democratic order? While homes and meeting places are searched for daring to say ’no‘ to war and militarization? While people are stripped of their citizenship because of a post on social media? While our comrades Zo, Leandra, Vi, Daniel and Crow are being subjected to a farce trial in Stammheim, the same place as the RAF?

Only last month, Akel D., a student of Wedding’s Berliner Hochschule fuer Technik was killed in Lebanon by an Israeli airstrike while visiting family, and the initiative to remember him and end university’s cooperation with apartheid was immediately subjected to surveillance and intimidation.

This is a test for all of us too: how much can we take? How long can we pretend that as long as we protest, but not too loud, we will be safe? That if we comply with the new normal, nothing will happen to us?

It’s time to say no! To turn solidarity into action! No conscription for our youth! No weapons for genocide! No police in our neighborhoods! Solidarity with the Ulm5 and free Palestine!

Let’s take to the streets – today, tomorrow, every day.

Self-organize! Desert! Sabotage!

WIR RUFEN ZUR ANARCHISTISCHEN BETEILIGUNG AUF:

Und nicht zu vergessen: Im März wurde das Haus in der Schererstraße, in dem wir und andere Gruppen uns treffen und organisieren, durchsucht.

Was wir hier beobachten, geschieht überall in Europa, wo ein Narrativ der permanenten Gefahr herangezogen wird, um die Idee zu rechtfertigen, dass Milliarden benötigt werden, um das Land gegen innere und äußere Feinde zu verteidigen.

Für diejenigen, die sich dem Kampf gegen Kriege, Besatzung und Militarisierung sowie gegen die erschreckende Normalisierung des seit drei Jahren live übertragenen Völkermords an den Palästinensern anschließen, ist Repression keine Frage von „Ob“, sondern „Wann“. author: Berlin Assembly in memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris and in solidarity with the anarchist comrades Marianna M. and Dimitra Z.
title: Imagination. Optimism. Risk. – two days solidarity fundraising
content:
On July 3rd and 4th we invite you to a 2-days event of discussion, music and other creative activities, combined with drinks and nice food. The purpose of this coming-together is to raise money in solidarity with imprisoned anarchist comrades in Greece from the Ampelokipoi case and with comrades here in Berlin who have been facing repression after soli-actions for the case.

End of April this year, while fighting in the courtroom for the memory of the anarchist fighter Kyriakos Xymitiris, who lost his life in the battle for social and class liberation on October 31st 2024, Marianna Manoura and Dimitra Zarafeta got sentenced to 19 and 8 years of prison in first instance in the context of the Ambelokipoi case in Athens.

Last year, on May 29th, the collective bar Meuterei was re-opened for some hours in its former space in Berlin. People gathered to enjoy a community moment, to show their anger about the gentrification of the neighbourhood and to defend the memory of Kyriakos. Cops showed up, kettled and arrested several dozen people. Some of the comrades who participated in the action recently received high charges.

The collected money will be used to cover the costs of the trials both in Athens and Berlin.

Our solidarity is non-negotiable. Our memories weave our present. They enable us to imagine the path of liberation of all and to take the risk to walk along that path. To nourish optimism and hope that one day we will win.

* Inspired by our fallen comrade.

Friday, July 3. Info event: The struggle continues – voices of (ex)prisoners and discussion about terrorism, internationalist struggles and solidarity.

There is a connection between the escalation of a global regime of war, collective responses from below, and the state’s application of anti-terrorism laws. In order to isolate and silence (resisting) people from movements and society, they are persecuted as terrorists or treated according to the same logic.

We see this with the anarchist prisoners Marianna and Dimitra in Athens, with the PalestineAction prisoners from the UK through the Czech Republic to Ulm, and with Palestinians worldwide. It is also a historical pattern, directed against the armed organizations that emerged from the ’68 movements in Western Europe.

On the one hand, we want to analyze what the current times — which we have described as the escalation of a global war regime — mean. On the other hand, we want to discuss what stance and what values we need for our struggles, which we must ground in a global perspective, with the prisoners at the forefront.

In this event, we would therefore like to hear from prisoners (via phone, in writing, or via voice message) and then hold a joint discussion. We want to bring together current and historical perspectives.

Where? Rigaer94 (Rigaerstr. 94, 10247 Berlin)

At 6:00 pm the call with Marianna and Dimitra will start.

The call will be followed by the voices of current and former prisoners in Germany and UK.

Live music: Hip hop performances, Yona Ro

Saturday, July 4: Kiezfest der Solidarität des Gedenkens

All-day gathering with nice food and drinks, live music and lots of creative activities (also for the youngest) in front of New Yorck Bethanien. We will use this day as a chance to come together as an open community around the memory of Kyriakos and actively show our solidarity to our imprisoned and accused comrades.

Where? In front of New Yorck Bethanien (Mariannenplatz 2a, 10997 Berlin)

Live music: Blanche Against the Machine, CALIKAÇAK, JAM Paradoxiaka.

There will also be a remembrance ceremony for our fallen comrade Kyriakos Xymitiris.

author: Brian Hioe
title: What Does Contention About Drones with the Pan-Blue Camp Indicate?
content:
THE KMT AND TPP have blocked committee review of a 210 billion NT special budget for drones, which would have funded domestic procurement of drones.

The special budget would have provided for the purchase of mostly maritime drones, consisting of 208,200 coastal attack drones, 1,446 coastal reconnaissance drones, and 1,320 uncrewed surface vessels. This occurs at a time when experts have warned that Taiwan needs to step up the number of drones it has available in the event of war scenarios, with Ukraine regularly expending tens of thousands of drones in combat with Russia.

For its part, the TPP and KMT have proposed their own versions of drone procurement legislation. The legislation proposed by the TPP and KMT aims to give require the legislature to sign off on further spending, giving the two parties more control over drone development initiatives in the future.

Previous TPP special budgets for military purchases had been criticized. First, TPP chair Huang Kuo-chang was accused of taking confidential documents of the Lai administration’s version of defense spending out of the meeting room in order to photograph them, so as to allow the TPP to draft its own version. Afterward, the version of the bill that was produced by the TPP was criticized as being amateurishly written, in that it limited arms purchases to 82 HIMARS multiple rocket launcher systems, 60 M109A self-propelled howitzers,  70 Javelin anti-tank missile systems, 24 TOW-2B anti-tank missile systems, as well as missile-firing drones.

Specifically, criticisms were that the version of the bill produced by the TPP did not conform to how arms procurement bills are normally written. As such, Taiwan would be limited to buying certain kinds of ammunition that it may not need, in that the only precision artillery it was allowed to buy is M109A artillery shells, potentially leading to shortages in terms of actual defense usage. The bill also did not provide funding for the storage or maintenance of equipment, which would lead to the degradation of such equipment, and still cut 70% of funding from defense spending.

As for the KMT, one notes that in past defense spending proposals, the KMT criticized the idea of purchasing arms from the US. Leaning into US-skeptic narratives increasingly in political circulation in Taiwan, the KMT claimed that the US was foisting useless arms onto Taiwan in order to politically profit, when they might not be genuinely useful for Taiwan’s defense.

But when the KMT eventually approved some level of defense spending, it still proved to be US weapons sales that were mostly allowed for. Domestic capabilities, such as drones, were cut –again, even if experts have increasingly taken the view that drones would be critical for the asymmetric defense that Taiwan needs to face a much larger enemy such as China.

For its part, the KMT has leaned into traditional narratives, suggesting that drones are a new and untested form of technology and that the DPP is attempting to push for drone technology merely to benefit drone companies to which it is close. The KMT has suggested that the companies that the DPP wishes to purchase drones from are unknown and are simply linked to the party.

Indeed, the KMT has leaned into such claims regarding everything from domestically developed and manufactured COVID-19 vaccines to green energy initiatives and Taiwan’s domestic submarine program. In this sense, the KMT has increasingly leaned into skepticism regarding Taiwan’s domestic capacities in addition to US-skepticism. Attacking the drone budget has been no different.

The Chinese government evidently views drones as a major threat to any invasion plans, and blocking drone funding opens the KMT up to accusations that it is taking directives from China so as to sabotage Taiwan’s defenses. Still, that the KMT and TPP were pressured into passing some form of drone spending probably speaks to public interest in the issue.

content:

Eigentümer der Firma „Nudelmann & Friends“ sind Benjamin Nudelmann und Jerry Padovicz. Während Benjamin neben seinen Immobiliengeschäften sich noch als freiwilliger Fallschirmjäger bei der IDF für das Morden und die Besatzung Palästinas eingesetzt hat, ist Jerry der Sohn von Giroja Padovicz, der neben der Räumung der Liebig34 noch unendlich viel weiteren Dreck am Stecken hat.

„Nudelmann & Friends“ ist auch die Firma, die die R94 kurz vor der Brandschutzbegehung als „unbewohnte Fläche“ anbot. Schon damals wurde eines seiner Gebäude Ziel einer Aktion.

Lassen wir dies eine Erinnerung an den angeblichen Eigentümer und alle um ihn herum sein, dass jeder Angriff oder Räumungsversuch mehr Schaden als Profit bringen wird!
R94 bleibt!

author: CNT Galiza
title: 3 al 31 de julio. Exposición tintA
content:
Desde sus inicios, el anarquismo optó por la cultura para difundir su concepción de un mundo nuevo: libre, justo, desprovisto de toda dominación y alcanzado mediante la transformación social. Desarrollando una amplia gama de prácticas y actividades culturales, los anarquistas no solo buscaban difundir la Idea, sino también satisfacer la sed de conocimiento del proletariado y el campesinado, privados en su gran mayoría del acceso a una formación educativa y cultural mínima. Escuelas racionalistas, ateneos, asambleas, teatro, publicaciones, grupos de lectura, artes gráficas, conferencias… el ámbito cultural del movimiento libertario se desarrolló ampliamente, conformando un proyecto heterogéneo y emancipador con identidad propia.

Entre toda esta multitud de manifestaciones culturales, la palabra escrita adquirió gran relevancia. Con enorme determinación y esfuerzo, surgieron boletines, panfletos, revistas, periódicos… una infinidad de publicaciones que rápidamente se arraigaron entre los estratos sociales más desfavorecidos.

Esta tradición cultural anarquista tuvo su momento de mayor esplendor en el Estado español durante la Revolución Social, donde innumerables publicaciones abordaron todo tipo de temas: geografía, filosofía, historia, sexualidad, pedagogía, etc. Con la derrota en la Guerra Civil y el establecimiento de la dictadura franquista, el número de publicaciones disminuyó drásticamente y su presencia se convirtió en un testimonio de la prohibición, respaldada por una sangrienta represión y el miedo, que imposibilitaba la publicación y difusión de cualquier idea que no fuera afín al régimen.

Tras la muerte del dictador en noviembre de 1975 y la perspectiva de un nuevo horizonte, el resurgimiento de la cultura libertaria recuperó impulso. Con la llegada y el auge del fanzine a finales de los setenta y principios de los ochenta, comienza un nuevo período extraordinariamente fértil, en el que el activismo anarquista encuentra en la autonomía y la libertad que ofrece esta publicación artesanal el medio perfecto para la difusión cultural e informativa de una realidad alternativa en plena confrontación con la hegemonía de los medios de comunicación de masas y la cultura oficial.

Papel, tijeras, pegamento… cortar y pegar, fotocopias y ¡tintA!

TintA es una muestra que reúne una pequeña selección de fanzines de entre la infinidad de publicaciones libertarias surgidas desde finales de los setenta hasta la actualidad, donde, a través de una serie de artículos seleccionados, nos acercaremos a la REALIDAD experiencial de una unión; de un ateneo; de una asociación cultural; de personas… Conoceremos sus puntos de vista, sus opiniones, sus inquietudes, sus luchas…

Puedes visitar esta exposición en A Coruña, del 3 al 31 de julio en el Círculo de Artesanos.

author: Omar Hassan
title: Hanson’s shadow looms over Victoria: a serious socialist campaign can galvanise a fightback
content:
The key question coming out of the November election will be not who wins, but how many people the socialist movement can win to our side in the face of Hanson’s fascistic tsunami.

The November Victorian election is shaping up as a decisive battle, the outcome of which will have ramifications well beyond the state. The surge of support for One Nation has created the real possibility that Victoria will be governed by a far-right coalition come December. The only real alternative—a fourth term for the current right-wing Labor government—is about as enticing as a reheated Big Mac.

In this dangerous situation, Victorian Socialists are planning the most serious election campaign attempted by a left party in decades. The party aims to disrupt the false binary that tells people there is no alternative but to choose between the status quo and the far right. Instead, Victorian Socialists want to offer working-class people across the state the chance to vote for a party that doesn’t advocate more of the same, and that equally doesn’t blame migrants or climate science for society’s problems. Victorian Socialists are offering a vision of society in which the interests of working-class people—the great majority—are prioritised over corporate greed and the market.

One Nation’s performance in the election will be decisive to the outcome and to the party’s wider momentum. Support for Hanson nationally has surged from just 6.5 percent in the last federal election to over 30 percent today—a startling development in a country where the two major parties have managed to dominate the electoral sphere even while many of their counterparts internationally have collapsed.

There has always been an organised far right in Australia, but, until recently, most of their would-be constituents have been prepared to stick with the Liberal and National parties. Those days are over. This constituency is radicalising, whipped into a frenzy by the Murdoch press and algorithms designed by social media executives. Hanson’s rise—funded and sponsored by a number of billionaire backers—has emboldened far-right freaks and intensified every pre-existing reactionary sentiment: Islam is a cancer; abortion is murder; left-wing protesters should be banned; climate change is rubbish; workers are overpaid, lazy and should be easier to sack.

These sorts of fascistic positions are now being sanitised if not openly promoted by Australia’s media establishment. Case in point: Hanson’s speech at the National Press Club, a prestigious forum that the media establishment like to think of as intellectually rigorous. There, she repeated all her far right talking points in a stumbling, blundering rant, and was praised to the rooftops for it.

“Hanson’s formidable Press Club performance proved her enemies wrong”, declared the Sydney Morning Herald. News.com.au described the tirade as evidence of “a politician ready to rule”. “Hanson is sharp in every sense, from her political antenna to her rhetoric”, gushed the associate editor of the Australian. Evidently, the media establishment, and the capitalist class it takes its lead from, are warming up to the prospect of a fascist government.

The establishment parties are not offering any real resistance either. Opposition leader Angus Taylor just puts Hanson’s speeches through Chat GPT with a filter for private school pomposity. Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson presents a more modern image in Victoria, but will likely preference and govern with Hanson if necessary.

Labor is rhetorically more oppositional but utterly cynical, championing multiculturalism while taking every opportunity to punch down, most recently by launching an Islamophobic trial by media of Muslim women and children fleeing prison camps in Syria. Meanwhile, Labor oversees a society in which banks, mining companies and bosses are getting rich at workers’ expense. Even when they do something vaguely progressive, like some of the measures in the budget, they can’t defend them when attacked from the right, instead abandoning some in the hope they will be left alone. This weak, hypocritical stance is exactly what creates the conditions that help the far right grow. The Greens try to challenge Hanson, but the party’s technocratic, pro-capitalist politics means it cannot lead the fight that’s needed.

Socialists have a totally different strategy to fight the far right. Unlike every other political party, which support and want to govern the same system One Nation does, we want to challenge capitalism and the ideology that underlies it. The mainstream parties can’t consistently oppose One Nation, because they too rely on bigotry and backwardness to deflect attention from the inequality, brutality and destructiveness of capitalism. and none of them are committed to building a fighting working-class movement that could win serious gain for workers, let alone smash the system. Such a movement, in their eyes, represents an intolerable threat to the status quo and the mainstream politicians’ privileged position within it.

The Victorian state election represents an important opportunity to mobilise and build the sort of socialist forces needed to challenge both the far right and Labor’s status quo. To resist the rise of Hansonism in our neighbourhoods and fight for a working-class politics based on solidarity and class struggle, Victorian Socialists will be organising thousands of volunteers to knock on hundreds of thousands of doors, with the goal of convincing working-class people that voting socialist is the best response to the shitshow that is Australian politics today.

We’re not the only ones preparing for this kind of mass campaign. Barnaby Joyce recently spoke at an anti-abortion rally in Sydney, explaining that the thing he needed most to defeat abortion rights was to build an army of people prepared to hand out how-to-vote cards. One Nation now has between 60,000 and 70,000 members nationwide, with more joining every week. They are setting themselves for an historic push to take power in Australia’s traditionally most left-wing state.

That some on the left continue to be squeamish about openly recruiting to socialism and organising people is a huge problem when the far right is rapidly signing up tens of thousands to its cause. We need to be thinking and acting on the same scale—it will take a socialist party of tens of thousands of working-class people to defeat this far right and the establishment that bred them. A party that is not a glorified email list, but a network of educators, agitators and organisers with serious roots in society.

This election campaign is a moment to take a big step towards building that kind of organisation. It is a chance to convince more workers than ever before to vote socialist and to join a movement to abolish capitalism and all the horrors it breeds. There is a real possibility that this movement could finally get a socialist elected to parliament, a voice for our class and for every movement against injustice.

It’s clear now that Hanson and her far right minions will win a significant and unprecedented share of the vote. While it would be a disaster if they were able to form some sort of coalition government, the re-election of Labor will only further fuel the far right’s growth. To change the equation in the long run, a stronger socialist movement is needed.

This means the key question coming out of this election will be not who wins, but how many people the socialist movement can win to our side in the face of Hanson’s fascistic tsunami. A strong result would offer a counter-narrative about the direction of society, indicating that there is a working-class left that wants transformative change. And a substantial growth and spread of the Socialist Party would put the left in a better position to fight, regardless of the outcome in November.

author: CNT Sabadell
title: Julio. Sabadell conmemora el 90 aniversario de la Revolución Social de 1936
content:
CNT Sabadell realizará una exposición sobre la unidad entre CNT y UGT, con motivo de los 90 años de la Revolución Social. Se desarrollará entre el 8 y el 25 de julio, siendo la mayoría de los actos en el Casal Pere Quart.

CNT Sabadell presenta el programa de actos para el 90 aniversario de la Revolución Social Conjuntamente con UGT. Los actos empezarán con la inauguración de la exposición de carteles “La imagen de la unidad”. Este año se cumplen 90 años de la proclamación de la Revolución Social, el 19 de julio de 1936.

Frustrado el golpe de estado de Franco, que dio inicio a la guerra civil, la CNT proclamó la revolución social y el comunismo libertario en todas aquellas zonas que no habían quedado bajo control de los sublevados. Lejos de ser una declaración espontánea, la CNT llevaba meses preparándose para la revolución social, como demuestra la atención que el comunismo libertario tuvo en el congreso de Zaragoza, celebrado dos meses antes.

Para conmemorar aquella revolución, única en el mundo, desde la CNT de Sabadell hemos preparado una serie de actos durante el mes de julio:

Con motivo del 90 aniversario de la revolución social, se presenta en Sabadell la exposición “La Imagen de la Unidad”, formada por una treintena de carteles de la época editados conjuntamente por las dos organizaciones sindicales más importantes del período, la CNT y la UGT.

A cargo de miembros de CNT, UGT y la Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo, se realizará un breve repaso de los principales hitos de la revolución social de 1936, principalmente la gestión de las fábricas por partes de los sindicatos y la colectivización de tierras. Asimismo, se realizará una breve visita guiada por la exposición.

El historiador sabadellense Josep Antoni Pozo realizará una visita comentada, donde explicará el contexto y los acontecimientos del período revolucionario, añadiendo anécdotas, curiosidades y documentos de la época.

Como tantas otras ciudades industriales, Sabadell permaneció bajo control obrero durante buena parte del período revolucionario. Aunque la conservación del patrimonio histórico no sea uno de los puntos fuertes de Sabadell, pasaremos por los escenarios principales de la revolución, explicados por el historiador sabadellense Arnau Berenguer, para acabar en el Ateneu Llibertari de Sabadell para hacer un vermut.

El historiador sabadellense Josep Antoni Pozo realizará una visita comentada, donde explicará el contexto y los acontecimientos del período revolucionario, añadiendo anécdotas, curiosidades y documentos de la época.

A pesar del alcance y magnitud de la revolución social y de los miles de hombres y mujeres implicadas, se trata de una historia silenciada. En 2014, y tras una campaña de micromecenazgo, se estrenó el documental Economía Colectiva, imprescindible para acercarse a la realidad de lo que supuso la gestión de la economía por parte de los sindicatos. Le invitamos a la proyección del documental con debate posterior.

«Concepto confederal del Comunismo Libertario»IV Congreso Confederal de CNTZaragoza, 1-10 de mayo de 1936.

En consecuencia, creemos que la revolución debe cimentarse sobre los principios sociales y éticos del Comunismo Libertario, que son:

Primero. Dar a cada ser humano lo que exigen sus necesidades, sino que en la satisfacción de las mismas tengan otras limitaciones que las posibilidades de la economía.

Segundo. Solicitar de cada ser humano la aportación máxima de sus esfuerzos a tenor de las necesidades de la sociedad, teniendo en cuenta las condiciones físicas y morales de cada individuo.

Terminado el aspecto violento de la revolución, se declararán abolidos: La propiedad privada, el Estado, el principio de autoridad y, por consiguiente, las clases que dividen a los hombres en explotadores y explotados, oprimidos y opresores.

Socializada la riqueza, las organizaciones de productoras, devenidos libres, se encargarán de la administración directa de la producción y el consumo.

author: Luca Tavan
title: Why are Australia’s union leaders the most enthusiastic defenders of the status quo?
content:
The ACTU acts as a lobby in reverse: rather than lobbying the government on behalf of its members, it lobbies its members on behalf of the government.

Everybody seems to agree that something has gone badly wrong for workers in Australia. Everybody, that is, except the leaders of the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU). Reading communications from the peak body representing Australian unions is like visiting an alternate universe in which we’ve never had it so good. Today’s top union leaders seem uniquely unmoved by the stagnating living standards and frustrated hopes that are driving popular anger at the status quo. Instead of organising a fight back, the ACTU acts like a meek liberal NGO. Worse, it acts as a lobby in reverse: rather than lobbying the government on behalf of its members, it lobbies its members on behalf of the government.

The fundamental issue in recent years is that wages have failed to keep up with inflation. After a decade of wage stagnation beginning in the early 2010s, real wages fell amid the supply shocks of the early 2020s. A series of below-inflation wage rulings and interest rate hikes has ensured that the costs of these shocks have been borne by workers. The Reserve Bank projects that it will take until 2028 before real wages return to 2011 levels—the biggest sustained drop in living standards anywhere in the OECD in recent times.

Add to this a broken housing system that means renters need an income of $130,000 for an average rental property to be deemed “affordable”. Plus, an underfunded health system results in half of people skipping necessary care. Through all this, ACTU leaders have maintained their enthusiasm for a government that has allowed workers’ living standards to nosedive.

Union leaders can’t credibly claim that their inaction reflects the prevailing sentiments among workers. A June Redbridge poll found a record 63 percent of people think that society is headed “in the wrong direction”. A recent ANUpoll found that 70 percent think the government should definitely or probably reduce income differences between the rich and the poor. Nearly 80 percent think that governments definitely or probably should provide decent housing for those who can’t afford it. No wonder young people are moving to the left in large numbers, and staying there.

The ACTU has hosted conference after conference about the importance of organising young workers. It’s obvious that the most basic way to do this would be to organise a massive campaign to raise wages. So why is ACTU Secretary Sally McManus instead lauding paltry nominal pay rises from the Fair Work Commission? McManus called the commission’s recent annual ruling a “positive real wage increase”, adding, “It means relief is on the way for lower-paid workers to help keep up with price pressures and avoid the need to cut back on essentials like food or seeing a doctor”.

While the leader of the workers’ movement focused on the purported positives, the Fair Work Commission itself said something substantially different:

The ACTU leaders have spent years promoting Labor’s piss-weak tweaks to tax and industrial legislation and assuring unionists that they don’t need to fight for anything better. ACTU communications read more like Labor ads than calls to action. Take the following:

A December 2022 email to union members promised: “New workplace laws will help get wages moving again”

Another, from June 2024, announced: “The Albanese government’s tax-cut plan ... will provide every Australian taxpayer with a cost-of-living bonus. That’s an extra $28 in their pocket each week”. The email added, with the energy of an infomercial presenter: “But that’s not all! The Albanese government’s Budget includes a $300 energy bill relief payment to every Australian household.” Forget that between 2023 and 2025, power costs surged 27 percent above the consumer price index.

A statement in June 2025 again touts as a “union win” a ruling to give 100,000 workers on the minimum wage a pay cut in real terms.

The same approach is embodied in the Victorian Trades Hall Council (VTHC), the representative body for Victorian unions. The VTHC describes itself as “the voice of Victorians at work”. But it doesn’t spend much time trying to find out what workers want or helping them raise their voices. The VTHC has bigger things to worry about—like turning over its headquarters to a massive effort to re-elect the unpopular state Labor government.

VTHC Secretary Luke Hilakari recently issued a public broadside against “complacent” Labor MPs. Don’t get too excited, though. The complacency Hilakari criticises them for has nothing to do with wages, schools or hospitals. He’s just upset that many of them are refusing to campaign seriously for another term in parliament. How urging absentee MPs to fight for another four years of seat-warming on the public purse counts as “union business” is anyone’s guess.

The job of selling Labor’s garbage offerings to workers is also taken on by affiliated unions.

The Australian Education Union leadership has been locked in a battle with its own members, urging them to accept a government offer that would have failed to address the crisis facing public schools. Right now, it’s a losing battle for the union leaders, in part because they blew much of their credibility by forcing through a massive pay cut in the last agreement.

Or take Labor’s 2026 federal budget, which contains $63.8 billion in cuts, including through the elimination of 28,000 public service jobs. At the centre is the government’s planned “overhaul” of the National Disability Insurance Scheme, which aims to save $36 billion. While the government has sold this as necessary to confront shonky private providers rorting the system, only $900 million of these cuts will come from crackdowns on fraud. The overwhelming majority of savings will come from cutting 240,000 people from the scheme.

Incredibly, the unions that represent the most workers in the disability care sector have helped to sell this. The Health Services Union initially celebrated the cuts as “a genuine turning point for the scheme” and “an important step in the right direction”. The Australian Services Union issued a mealy-mouthed statement that euphemistically referred to funding “changes”, while its social media commentary described the budget as “massive slay”.

Many union leaders also act as enforcers for the bosses. They can be in blatantly right-wing unions such as the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association, which has a record of colluding with the supermarket giants to slash penalty rates. They can also be in supposedly progressive unions such as the National Tertiary Education Union, which in recent years proposed a Jobs Protection Framework that would have allowed university bosses to slash wages by 15 percent.

How did the leaders of the union movement become cheerleaders for such a crap state of affairs? Why are they so indifferent to attacks on their members?

First, the decline in working-class living standards and weakening of union power haven’t affected the lives of those who lead the unions. Sally McManus takes home more than $200,000 a year—and she is far from the highest-paid union leader. United Firefighters Union National Secretary Peter Marshall’s annual salary averages around half a million dollars. The Australian Education Union’s Victorian branch president, Justin Mullaly, is preaching prudence to teachers fighting to catch up on years of lost pay, but receives an annual package of $228,678.

Just as MPs who pass legislation to gut school and health funding receive salaries that insulate them and their families from the impact of those decisions, so too are union officials inoculated against the effect of declining wages and workplace organisation.

As union activism has declined, generating fewer trade union militants with real organisational experience, the ranks of the union bureaucracy have been increasingly drawn from the middle classes. Unions today are more often than not staffed by former lawyers or student politicians. Past Labor leader Bill Shorten’s path is typical—from joining Labor at Monash University, he volunteered and served as an adviser for various Labor MPs, then got a job in a Labor-aligned law firm, before working his way up the ranks to lead the Australian Workers’ Union.

Just as important as the social origins and pay packets of union leaders are the opportunities that come from their proximity to power. There is a well-worn path from union offices to parliamentary benches and beyond. The current deputy prime minister, Richard Marles, was an assistant secretary of the ACTU; Greg Combet was parachuted from ACTU secretary to Rudd-era defence personnel minister. Some, like Martin Ferguson, go even further. From being president of the ACTU, he leapt to opposition benches in 1996, before later becoming the resources and energy minister, and going on to plum jobs at Channel 7, BP and various industry groups. He has spent the last decade advocating for expanded uranium mining, energy privatisation and wage cuts—all while remaining a paid-up Labor member! You really can have it all.

This revolving door reflects and reinforces the approach to unionism that has dominated since the 1980s: prioritising proximity to government and business—having a “seat at table”—over organising workers collectively. This is why union leaders urge loyalty to institutions such as the Fair Work Commission, which they claim can replace strike action with “expert” decisions made by ruling-class judges and economists.

It also means that maintenance of a Labor government is always a top priority for union leaders. No wonder they pull so many punches when Labor attacks union members, and attempt to generate hype for so many meaningless and symbolic Labor policies. This is an especially marked problem today when the most unionised workforces—nurses, teachers, civil servants—are in the public sector, meaning their employer is the same government that the union leaders are often unwilling to challenge.

Finally, to stay in the good graces of the powerful, union leaders frequently try to prove they can act as industrial police, imposing discipline and sacrifice on their members.

Take the aforementioned NTEU Jobs Protection Framework debacle. In explaining the rationale for this proposal at an RMIT University Q&A session, Secretary Matt McGowan said that the framework would give the union “a form of authority that it hasn’t had in over three decades ... And this will significantly improve the union’s ability to impact on the future structure and direction of the sector”. Translation: they were willing to trade away their members’ conditions for more influence for themselves. Thankfully, the proposal was defeated by a rebellion among the members.

Even after decades in which union leaders have managed the decline of their institutions while eroding workers’ consciousness and expectations, there is still a willingness to fight for something better when an opportunity arises. The current campaign of Victorian public-school teachers to catch up on years of lost pay shows this. In March, 35,000 teachers participated in a historic strike rally. Thousands of teachers choking Melbourne’s CBD and shutting down a vital service was a vivid illustration that unions are still the largest, and potentially most powerful, organisations of social change.

Since then, the battle has been against not just the state Labor government but also the leaders of the education union. The victory for a “no” vote against the latest offer, underpinned by determined campaigning by socialists in the union, shows that the union leaders don’t always get their way.

The model of unionism that socialists argue for in the teachers’ union—based on collective action rather than lobbying, on raising people’s expectations rather than telling them to accept crumbs—will be an essential part of rebuilding a left pole of opposition to the status quo. This is the only way we can start to shift the dial towards a society that puts workers first, rather than the rich and powerful.

author: cnt.es
title: 10 de julio. Presentación de ‘La libertad contra la autoridad’, antología de textos de Mijaíl Bakunin
content:
El próximo 10 de julio, a las 19:30, se presenta en la Biblioteca “Sebastián Oliva” de la CNT de Jerez, La libertad contra la autoridad, antología de textos del anarquista ruso que ha preparado Jordi Maíz en el 150 aniversario de su fallecimiento.

Figura central del anarquismo del siglo XIX y pensador clave para comprender las rupturas del socialismo frente a sus vertientes autoritarias, Mijaíl Bakunin se presenta en esta obra a través de una biografía breve y una cuidada selección de textos esenciales. El volumen recorre la trayectoria vital e intelectual de un revolucionario que desafió las ortodoxias de su tiempo, enfrentándose a Marx y a los defensores de un socialismo centralizado, y apostando por una transformación radical y libertaria de la sociedad. Los escritos escogidos permiten adentrarse en cuestiones fundamentales como la crítica al Estado, el rechazo de toda forma de jerarquía política, la importancia de la acción colectiva espontánea, el papel del campesinado en la revolución, la educación y la defensa de la libertad individual como principio irrenunciable. El libro incluye también estudios actualizados para quienes deseen profundizar en el pensamiento bakuninista y su persistente influencia en diversas tradiciones emancipadoras.

¿Cuándo? Viernes 10 de julio¿Dónde? Biblioteca “Sebastián Oliva” de la CNT de Jerez¿Horario? 19:00

author: CNT Colmenar Viejo
title: 17 de julio. La Revolución Social de 1936 en Colmenar
content:
El 17 de julio, viernes, a las 20 h, queremos hacer un homenaje a la Revolución Social de 1936 con motivo de los 90 años de este acontecimiento que marcó la historia de España.

Tenemos la suerte de contar con nuestro compañero Roberto Fernández Suárez, historiador y antropólogo conocedor de estos acontecimientos que nos contará los sucesos de aquellos días.

Después de la charla tendremos cena y picoteo y para terminar un poco de música y bailoteo, que ya sabéis, cómo diría Emma Goldman: “Si no hay baile, no es mi Revolución”.

La importancia que tuvo Colmenar Viejo en estos tiempos fue más que notable, pues al fracasar la sublevación militar en Madrid, Colmenar Viejo se convirtió en un enclave destacado de la retaguardia republicana durante la guerra.

Se hablará de la importancia que tuvo la CNT de esta localidad en la persecución de sus objetivos libertarios: una economía colectivizada, impulsar una gobernanza descentralizada con el protagonismo de diferentes comités que se crearon para administrar la vida cotidiana del pueblo, fomentar la creación y desarrollo de una escuela racionalista para la población infantil, participar en la nueva prensa local, dirigir las milicias antifascistas de la localidad. En definitiva, destacaremos aquellas iniciativas que pueden considerarse como el núcleo de la experiencia revolucionaria que se vivió intensamente en Colmenar Viejo como en el resto del país.

author: anred
title: Repudian las declaraciones de Clara Muzzio contra la ESI, las diversidades y las infancias trans
content:
Organizaciones, docentes, activistas y referentxs de derechos humanos impulsan una campaña de adhesiones para repudiar las declaraciones de la vicejefa de Gobierno porteño, Clara Muzzio, a quien acusan de promover discursos de odio, desinformar sobre la Educación Sexual Integral (ESI) y vulnerar derechos reconocidos por la legislación vigente. Por ANRed

Las recientes declaraciones de la vicejefa de Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, Clara Muzzio, generaron un amplio rechazo de organizaciones sociales, educativas y de derechos humanos. Durante una entrevista, la funcionaria afirmó que «hay dos sexos: el masculino y el femenino, y uno nace con eso», sostuvo que la Educación Sexual Integral (ESI) «le destrozó la cabeza a los niños», calificó a la ESI como una «ideología siniestra» y negó la existencia de las personas trans.

En respuesta, diversas organizaciones difundieron un pronunciamiento público titulado «Repudio a las declaraciones contra las diversidades y las infancias de la vicejefa de Gobierno porteño Clara Muzzio», que reúne adhesiones y denuncia el carácter discriminatorio de las expresiones de la funcionaria.

«Lxs abajo firmantes manifestamos nuestro enérgico repudio a las recientes declaraciones públicas de la Vicejefa de Gobierno porteño, Clara Muzzio, en las que ataca el derecho a la identidad de género, a la Educación Sexual Integral (ESI) y descalifica las infancias diversas bajo la etiqueta de ‘ideología woke'», expresa el documento.

El texto sostiene que las declaraciones, realizadas desde una alta responsabilidad institucional, «resultan maliciosas y discriminatorias, promotoras del odio y la violencia contra las identidades diversas», además de presentar una visión distorsionada del desarrollo infantil y vulnerar derechos garantizados por leyes nacionales y de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.

Las organizaciones firmantes también exigen la plena implementación de la Educación Sexual Integral, con contenidos laicos, científicos y respetuosos de las diversidades sexuales y de género en todos los niveles educativos porteños, junto con presupuesto suficiente para su aplicación efectiva y el respeto de los derechos sexuales y reproductivos en el sistema de salud de la Ciudad.

La respuesta desde la comunidad educativa

Frente a las afirmaciones de Muzzio, docentes y referentes de la ESI remarcaron que la Educación Sexual Integral no busca definir identidades ni promover estereotipos, sino garantizar derechos y brindar herramientas para el cuidado y la convivencia democrática.

En ese sentido, desde la comunidad ESI en Secundaria difundieron un texto en el que desmienten una de las frases utilizadas para desacreditar la política educativa: la idea de que la ESI le diría a un niño que juega con una muñeca que «nació en un cuerpo equivocado».

«La frase es falsa. Pero, sobre todo, es interesante. Porque la ESI jamás podría decir algo así. Hacerlo sería reforzar exactamente el estereotipo que busca desarmar: creer que un juguete puede decirnos quién es una persona», señalaron.

El documento advierte que adjudicarle a la ESI afirmaciones que nunca sostuvo construye una caricatura destinada a generar miedo y desinformación. «Mientras discutimos eso, dejamos de hablar de la ESI real: la que trabaja sobre derechos, cuidados, afectividad, consentimiento, prevención de las violencias, diversidad y pensamiento crítico», sostienen.

Finalmente, convocan a responder frente a las campañas de desinformación mediante el conocimiento de los lineamientos oficiales y la defensa de una educación basada en derechos. «La mejor respuesta frente a la desinformación sigue siendo la misma: más educación», concluye el texto.

Mientras continúa la recolección de adhesiones al pronunciamiento, organizaciones y docentes advierten que los discursos estigmatizantes emitidos por funcionarios públicos no solo desconocen el marco legal vigente, sino que contribuyen a profundizar la discriminación hacia las personas LGBTIQ+ y las infancias diversas.

author: anred
title: Paro docente en la provincia de Buenos Aires: gremios realizaron una jornada de lucha por salarios, contra la violencia en las escuelas y en defensa de la educación pública
content:
Los sindicatos AMET, FEB, SUTEBA y UDOCBA llevaron adelante este martes 30 de junio un paro docente provincial que, según las organizaciones gremiales, alcanzó un 95% de adhesión en todo el territorio bonaerense. La jornada estuvo acompañada por clases públicas, semaforazos, volanteadas, «trenazos» y presentaciones en jefaturas distritales, consejos escolares y concejos deliberantes. La medida reclamó la urgente convocatoria a paritarias, la restitución del FONID, políticas para abordar la violencia en las escuelas, el rechazo al desfinanciamiento de la educación técnica y el fin de la sobrecarga laboral docente. Por ANRed

En un escenario marcado por el deterioro del poder adquisitivo de los salarios docentes y el ajuste sobre la educación pública, el Frente de Unidad Docente Bonaerense (FUDB), integrado por AMET, FEB, SUTEBA y UDOCBA, llevó adelante este martes 30 de junio un paro provincial bajo la consigna «¡Basta de violencias! Urgente convocatoria a paritaria por aumento salarial».

Las organizaciones sindicales señalaron que la medida de fuerza respondió a la falta de respuestas frente a una serie de reclamos que vienen sosteniendo desde hace meses. En un comunicado conjunto afirmaron que el conflicto se desarrolló en un contexto de «ahogo financiero» hacia la provincia de Buenos Aires por parte del Gobierno Nacional, sumado a un «brutal ajuste» sobre la educación pública. Sin embargo desde SUTEBA multicolor, señalan las responsabilidades del gobernador de la provincia de Buenos Aires, Axel Kicillof.

Uno de los principales ejes del paro fue el creciente clima de violencia que atraviesan las instituciones educativas. Los gremios reclamaron la plena implementación del Acuerdo Paritario de Prevención, Erradicación, Resguardo y Reparación, la elaboración de un protocolo complementario, la realización de jornadas institucionales específicas y la aplicación de la legislación vigente para sancionar los hechos de violencia. También exigieron políticas concretas que garanticen la integridad física y psicológica de docentes, estudiantes y del conjunto de la comunidad educativa.

En materia salarial, las organizaciones demandaron la inmediata convocatoria a paritarias por parte del gobierno bonaerense y la restitución del Fondo Nacional de Incentivo Docente (FONID), eliminado por el Gobierno Nacional. Sostuvieron que la pérdida del poder adquisitivo continúa deteriorando las condiciones de vida de las y los trabajadores de la educación.

El documento también denunció la creciente sobrecarga laboral que enfrentan las y los docentes. En ese sentido, los sindicatos reclamaron el respeto por la jornada laboral y el derecho a la desconexión digital, además de modificaciones al Régimen Académico que eviten la extensión permanente de las tareas fuera del horario de trabajo. Asimismo, expresaron su rechazo a las resoluciones 3367 y 333 y reafirmaron la consigna «Ningún/a docente sin trabajo», frente al impacto que genera la baja de la matrícula escolar.

Entre los puntos del reclamo también figuró el rechazo al desfinanciamiento de la educación técnico-profesional. Las organizaciones exigieron que el Gobierno Nacional restituya las partidas presupuestarias destinadas al sostenimiento de las escuelas técnicas, al considerar que los recortes comprometen la formación de miles de estudiantes.

Los gremios manifestaron además su preocupación por las reformas previsionales impulsadas a nivel nacional, que, según advirtieron, podrían afectar el funcionamiento del IPS y los derechos jubilatorios de las y los trabajadores bonaerenses. También reclamaron mejoras urgentes en las prestaciones de IOMA para garantizar una cobertura adecuada al sector docente.

Al cierre de la jornada, AMET, FEB, SUTEBA y UDOCBA ratificaron su compromiso con la defensa de la educación pública y sostuvieron que continuarán impulsando medidas para exigir salarios dignos, condiciones laborales adecuadas y políticas públicas que garanticen el derecho a enseñar y aprender en escuelas seguras.
